terms.name: Canonical Identifier
terms.definition: A stable identifier owned by the canonical contract layer. Independent of any one source system; not changed when source systems re-key, merge, or migrate.

terms.name: System Identity Column
terms.definition: The immutable, system-generated GUID that is the primary key on every entity and codeset contract. Field name follows the pattern `*_uid`. Used as the join key for every relationship.

terms.name: Business Key
terms.definition: A human-readable identifier the business or operations assigns to an entity, such as a policy number, claim number, or submission number. Required where the business assigns one. Stored alongside the system identity column but not used as the canonical primary key.

terms.name: Source System Code
terms.definition: A code identifying the upstream system that produced or last asserted a canonical record. Captured for multi-source mastering and lineage; does not replace the system identity column.

terms.name: Source Natural Key
terms.definition: The natural key assigned by the source system. Captured for provenance and reconciliation; not used as the canonical primary key.

terms.name: Business Time
terms.definition: The time dimension that describes when a business concept is or was effective in the real world. Examples: a policy term's `term_effective_date` and `term_expiration_date`, a coverage's `effective_date`.

terms.name: System Time
terms.definition: The time dimension that describes when the canonical record was valid in the warehouse. Captured through SCD2 fields independent of business-time fields.

terms.name: Valid From Datetime
terms.definition: The system-time start of an SCD2 record version. Populated for every record version on every entity and codeset contract.

terms.name: Valid To Datetime
terms.definition: The system-time end of an SCD2 record version. Null indicates the current row.

terms.name: Is Current Indicator
terms.definition: A boolean that is true for exactly one row per logical key, indicating the current canonical record version.

terms.name: SCD2 Window
terms.definition: The pair of `valid_from_datetime` and `valid_to_datetime` that defines the time interval during which a record version was current in the warehouse.

terms.name: Bi-Temporal Model
terms.definition: A model that preserves both business time and system time. Required because insurance routinely backdates and corrects records, so the answers to "what was effective" and "what we knew, when" are different and both must be answerable.

terms.name: Record Status
terms.definition: The warehouse-level state of a canonical record, distinct from any business lifecycle status the entity may also carry. Captured in `record_status_code` on every entity contract.

terms.name: Active Record
terms.definition: A record whose `record_status_code` is `ACTIVE`. The default state for every newly written record.

terms.name: Superseded Record
terms.definition: A record version whose `record_status_code` is `SUPERSEDED` because a later version of the same logical key has taken its place.

terms.name: Soft-Deleted Record
terms.definition: A record whose `record_status_code` is `SOFT_DELETED` because the upstream truth is that the record should not have existed (data-entry error, duplicate, or system-of-record retraction). Soft delete is the only delete; rows are not physically removed from canonical contracts.

terms.name: Restated Record
terms.definition: A record whose `record_status_code` is `RESTATED` because the canonical interpretation has been revised even though the record itself is still considered to have existed.

terms.name: Merged Record
terms.definition: A record whose `record_status_code` is `MERGED` because the entity it represented has been consolidated into another canonical record. Carries `merged_into_uid` to point at the surviving record.

terms.name: Lifecycle Event
terms.definition: An append-only canonical record of a business-meaningful state change in an entity's history. Captures *what happened*. Does not by itself imply financial impact or processing.

terms.name: Transaction
terms.definition: An append-only canonical record of a unit of business activity that has financial impact, document generation, or independent processing identity. Captures *what was processed*.

terms.name: Correction Indicator
terms.definition: A boolean on every event and transaction record. True when the row corrects a previously emitted row, false otherwise. Original rows are immutable; corrections are emitted as new rows.

terms.name: Corrects Reference
terms.definition: The reference field (named `corrects_*_uid`) that points from a correcting event or transaction to the prior row it corrects. Populated only when the correction indicator is true.

terms.name: Triggering Transaction Reference
terms.definition: The optional reference on a lifecycle event that points to the transaction that produced the event, when the event is the consequence of a processed transaction rather than its cause.

terms.name: Codeset
terms.definition: A small, governed reference-data contract that enumerates the allowed values for a coded field, their human-readable labels, optional external-standard mappings, and their effective windows.

terms.name: Code Value
terms.definition: The business-friendly code value that an entity contract's `*_code` field references. Treated as the canonical foreign key into a codeset.

terms.name: Code Label
terms.definition: The human-readable name of a code value, used for presentation and reporting.

terms.name: External Standard Code
terms.definition: The code value as defined by an external standard (such as ACORD, NAIC, ISO 4217, or ISO 3166-2) when the canonical codeset records a mapping to that standard.

terms.name: Allowed Value
terms.definition: A code value that currently exists in the codeset and is valid for use. Adding an allowed value is a non-breaking change; removing or renaming one is breaking.

terms.name: Sentinel Code
terms.definition: An explicit codeset value used to distinguish "unknown" or "not applicable" from missing data. Used in place of overloading null when the business needs the distinction.

terms.name: Data Classification
terms.definition: Field-level metadata that captures the sensitivity tier and any applicable regulatory tags for a property. Used by downstream targets to enforce masking, row-level security, retention, and lineage tagging.

terms.name: Sensitivity Tier
terms.definition: The classification of how sensitive a field is. One of `PUBLIC`, `INTERNAL`, `CONFIDENTIAL`, or `RESTRICTED`. Every property declares one explicitly.

terms.name: Regulatory Tag
terms.definition: A tag indicating regulatory category. Includes `PII`, `PHI`, `PCI`, `SPI`, `FINANCIAL`, and `JURISDICTION_RESTRICTED`. Applied additively where multiple categories apply.

terms.name: Classification Profile
terms.definition: A contract-level summary of the most-sensitive class present on any property in the contract. Used by target generators to set the default sensitivity label on the materialized table.

terms.name: Subject To HIPAA
terms.definition: A contract-level flag that is true when any property is tagged with `PHI`. Used by downstream targets to branch into HIPAA-aware generation logic.

terms.name: Transactional Currency
terms.definition: The currency in which a monetary amount was originally booked. Stored on every monetary field through a sibling `*_currency_code` reference to the `CurrencyCode` codeset.

terms.name: House Currency
terms.definition: A reporting or presentation currency selected by a consumer for aggregation. Not represented in canonical contracts; computed downstream.

terms.name: Currency Pairing
terms.definition: The convention that every monetary field is paired with a `*_currency_code` field naming the currency of that amount. Required by the canonical layer; enforced by quality rules.

terms.name: Contract Version
terms.definition: The SemVer identifier on every contract: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Major bumps signal breaking changes for consumers, minor bumps signal additive changes, patch bumps signal documentation-only changes.

terms.name: Pre-Stable Version
terms.definition: A contract whose version is below `1.0.0`. Breaking changes are permitted between `0.x` minor versions but must still be recorded in the contract changelog.

terms.name: Changelog
terms.definition: The list of version entries on every contract, captured under `customProperties.changelog`. Each entry records date, change type, and brief description.

terms.name: Contract Status
terms.definition: The lifecycle position of a contract: `draft`, `proposed`, `approved`, `deprecated`, or `retired`. Promotion is gated by criteria documented in `status-promotion.md`.

terms.name: Deprecated Contract
terms.definition: A contract that is still emitted but discouraged because a successor exists. Carries deprecation metadata pointing at the replacement.

terms.name: Retired Contract
terms.definition: A contract that is no longer emitted. The contract file remains in the repository for historical reference but produces no target artifacts.

terms.name: Domain Steward
terms.definition: The named owner of a contract who signs off on promotion to `approved` and on subsequent changes that affect consumers.

terms.name: Canonical Layer
terms.definition: The Silver-layer position in the medallion architecture. The contracts in this repository define the canonical layer; Bronze landing and Gold mart shapes are downstream concerns.

terms.name: Source-Neutral
terms.definition: The property of a canonical contract that it does not embed source-system structure, vendor schema, raw DDL, ontology export, or copied definition. Source signal is allowed as design input only.

terms.name: Platform-Neutral
terms.definition: The property of a canonical contract that it does not embed target-platform mechanics. Target-specific projection (dbt, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake) lives under `targets/`.

terms.name: Claim
terms.definition: A record of loss, damage, injury, liability, or other covered or potentially covered event being handled under a Property and Casualty insurance context.

terms.name: Claim Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on a claim record (`claim_uid`). An immutable GUID used as the join key for every reference to the claim.

terms.name: Claim Number
terms.definition: The business-friendly identifier the business or operations assigns to a claim. Distinct from the claim identifier; not used as the primary key or relationship join key.

terms.name: Claim Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a claim.

terms.name: Claim Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of claim being handled.

terms.name: Loss Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of loss associated with a claim.

terms.name: Policy Context
terms.definition: The policy connected to a claim when the claim can be tied to policy coverage.

terms.name: Claim Coverage Context
terms.definition: The policy coverage connected to claim handling when coverage association is known.

terms.name: Claim Exposure Context
terms.definition: The exposure connected to claim handling when the risk basis is known.

terms.name: Loss Location
terms.definition: The location associated with the loss or event giving rise to the claim.

terms.name: Loss Date
terms.definition: The date when the loss occurred or is treated as having occurred.

terms.name: Reported Datetime
terms.definition: The date and time when the claim or loss was reported.

terms.name: Opened Date
terms.definition: The date when claim handling was opened.

terms.name: Closed Date
terms.definition: The date when claim handling was closed.

terms.name: Catastrophe Code
terms.definition: A code used to associate a claim with a catastrophe or large event grouping.

terms.name: Catastrophe Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that the claim is associated with a catastrophe or large event grouping.

terms.name: Litigation Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that the claim involves litigation or litigation handling.

terms.name: Claim Description
terms.definition: A source-neutral business description of the claim or loss context.

terms.name: Loss Notice
terms.definition: The initial notification that a loss or potential claim has occurred.

terms.name: Reserve Change
terms.definition: A change in expected claim financial responsibility or reserve amount.

terms.name: Recovery
terms.definition: Money or value recovered in connection with a claim.

terms.name: Salvage
terms.definition: Value recovered from damaged property associated with a claim.

terms.name: Subrogation
terms.definition: Recovery activity against another party that may be responsible for a loss.

terms.name: Reopen
terms.definition: An event or state where a previously closed claim becomes active again.

terms.name: Claim Feature
terms.definition: A partition of a claim into independent handling streams when distinct coverages, perils, or claimants are handled separately on a single claim. Optional; used by carriers that model feature-level handling.

terms.name: Feature Number
terms.definition: A business-friendly identifier for a feature within a claim. Distinct from the system identity column on the feature record.

terms.name: Feature Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a claim feature.

terms.name: Cause Of Loss
terms.definition: The classification of what caused the loss associated with a claim or claim feature. Captured through the `CauseOfLossCode` codeset.

terms.name: Claim Coverage
terms.definition: The connection between claim handling and the policy coverage that responds to the claim. Many-to-one from claim feature to policy coverage when features are used; many-to-many between claim and policy coverage when no feature partition is in place.

terms.name: Coverage Decision
terms.definition: The disposition recorded for the policy coverage's response to the claim, such as accepted, partially accepted, denied, or pending.

terms.name: Applicable Limit
terms.definition: The limit amount applied or available under a particular coverage response on a claim. Paired with a currency code.

terms.name: Applicable Deductible
terms.definition: The deductible amount applied under a particular coverage response on a claim. Paired with a currency code.

terms.name: Claim Lifecycle Event
terms.definition: A meaningful state change in the claim history. Examples include FNOL received, acknowledged, assigned, reserved, partial payment, full payment, closed, reopened, subrogation initiated, salvage initiated, denied, and withdrawn. Append-only; corrections are emitted as new immutable rows.

terms.name: FNOL
terms.definition: First Notice of Loss. The lifecycle event that records the initial notification of a loss or potential claim.

terms.name: Claim Party Role
terms.definition: The participation of a party in a claim context, such as claimant, insured contact, adjuster, supervisor, attorney, expert, witness, service provider, or recovery party.

terms.name: Adjuster
terms.definition: A party role on a claim that handles investigation, evaluation, and resolution.

terms.name: Claimant
terms.definition: A party role on a claim that asserts a claim against an insured or insurer.

terms.name: Service Provider
terms.definition: A party role on a claim that performs repair, medical, legal, or other services in connection with the claim.

terms.name: Recovery Party
terms.definition: A party role on a claim that is the source or target of a recovery, such as a subrogated party or a salvage purchaser.

terms.name: Claim Document
terms.definition: A document associated with a claim or claim feature. Stores metadata only; document content is held in an external store referenced through an opaque storage reference.

terms.name: External Storage Reference
terms.definition: An opaque pointer to document content held outside the canonical contract layer. The document body is never stored in the canonical contract.

terms.name: Contains PHI Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that a claim document is known to contain Protected Health Information. Used by downstream targets to apply HIPAA-compliant handling.

terms.name: Claim Financial Transaction
terms.definition: Append-only canonical record of a financial movement attached to a claim, such as reserves, payments, recoveries, salvage, subrogation, deductible recovery, or expense activity. Specializes the financial-transaction pattern with claim, feature, coverage, payee party role, and reserve-category context.

terms.name: Reserve Category
terms.definition: The classification of a reserve a financial transaction affects, such as indemnity reserve or expense reserve.

terms.name: Payee Party Role
terms.definition: The claim party role that is the payee of a financial transaction when the transaction transfers value to a party.

terms.name: Indemnity
terms.definition: The portion of claim cost that compensates for the loss itself, distinct from expense costs incurred to handle the claim.

terms.name: ALAE
terms.definition: Allocated Loss Adjustment Expense. Expense activity directly attributable to a specific claim, distinct from indemnity.

terms.name: ULAE
terms.definition: Unallocated Loss Adjustment Expense. Expense activity associated with claim handling that cannot be allocated to a specific claim.

terms.name: Catastrophe
terms.definition: A large event grouping that aggregates many claims arising from a single occurrence such as a hurricane, wildfire, or flood. Captured through the catastrophe code on a claim and reinforced by the catastrophe indicator.

terms.name: Party
terms.definition: A reusable identity for a person, organization, household, trust, public entity, or other recognized participant in Property and Casualty insurance activity.

terms.name: Party Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on a party record (`party_uid`). An immutable GUID generated upstream and used as the join key for every reference to the party. Distinct from any business-friendly identifier the source systems may assign.

terms.name: Party Type
terms.definition: A classification that describes the kind of party represented, such as person, organization, household, trust, or other recognized party type.

terms.name: Party Display Name
terms.definition: The business-facing name used to identify a party in operational and analytical contexts.

terms.name: Legal Name
terms.definition: The formal name for a party when contractual, regulatory, or legal context requires it.

terms.name: Person Party
terms.definition: A party that represents an individual human being.

terms.name: Organization Party
terms.definition: A party that represents a company, agency, carrier, employer, vendor, public entity, or other organized body.

terms.name: Party Role
terms.definition: The participation of a party in a specific business context, separated from the reusable party identity.

terms.name: Role Type
terms.definition: A classification of what a party does in a business context, such as insured, claimant, agent, producer, adjuster, beneficiary, employer, or vendor.

terms.name: Business Context
terms.definition: The business subject in which a party role applies, such as submission, policy, claim, account, agreement, coverage, or exposure.

terms.name: Context Identifier
terms.definition: The canonical identifier of the business context where a party role applies.

terms.name: Primary Role
terms.definition: The party role treated as the main role of its type within a business context.

terms.name: Party Relationship
terms.definition: A durable relationship between two parties that is not limited to one submission, policy, claim, or other single business context.

terms.name: Relationship Direction
terms.definition: The orientation of a party relationship from one party to another party.

terms.name: Relationship Type
terms.definition: A classification of the business meaning of a party-to-party relationship.

terms.name: Effective Date
terms.definition: The date when a record, role, relationship, value, or classification becomes valid for canonical business use.

terms.name: Expiration Date
terms.definition: The date when a record, role, relationship, value, or classification stops being valid for canonical business use.

terms.name: Party Role Type
terms.definition: The classification of a role a party plays in a business context, such as insured, claimant, producer, broker, agent, adjuster, loss payee, service provider, or underwriter. Captured through the `PartyRoleTypeCode` codeset.

terms.name: Effective Window
terms.definition: The pair of effective and expiration dates that bounds when a party identity, party role, or party relationship is valid for canonical business use. Distinct from the SCD2 system-time window.

terms.name: Coverage
terms.definition: A reusable insurance protection concept that can be offered, selected, or applied in a policy context.

terms.name: Coverage Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on a coverage record (`coverage_uid`). An immutable GUID used as the join key for every reference to the reusable coverage definition.

terms.name: Coverage Code
terms.definition: A business code that identifies a coverage concept.

terms.name: Coverage Name
terms.definition: The business-facing name for a coverage concept.

terms.name: Coverage Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of protection or obligation represented by a coverage.

terms.name: Coverage Category
terms.definition: A broader grouping used to organize related coverage concepts.

terms.name: Policy Coverage
terms.definition: Coverage selected, required, or applied within a policy, policy term, or exposure context.

terms.name: Coverage Sequence Number
terms.definition: A sequence used to order or distinguish coverages within a policy context.

terms.name: Coverage Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a coverage or policy-applied coverage.

terms.name: Coverage Level
terms.definition: The level at which coverage applies, such as policy, term, exposure, location, vehicle, or other recognized context.

terms.name: Coverage Basis
terms.definition: The basis used to determine how coverage applies or is measured.

terms.name: Selected Coverage
terms.definition: Coverage chosen or accepted for a policy context.

terms.name: Mandatory Coverage
terms.definition: Coverage required by product, jurisdiction, business rule, or policy structure.

terms.name: Policy Limit
terms.definition: Structured detail that defines the maximum amount, quantity, or unit of protection associated with a policy coverage.

terms.name: Limit Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of limit, such as occurrence, aggregate, per person, per item, or another recognized limit type.

terms.name: Limit Basis
terms.definition: The basis used to apply or evaluate a limit.

terms.name: Limit Amount
terms.definition: The monetary maximum associated with a policy limit.

terms.name: Limit Quantity
terms.definition: A non-monetary maximum associated with a policy limit.

terms.name: Limit Unit
terms.definition: The unit of measure for a non-monetary policy limit.

terms.name: Policy Deductible
terms.definition: Structured detail that defines the amount, percentage, or basis retained before coverage responds.

terms.name: Deductible Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of deductible associated with a policy coverage.

terms.name: Deductible Basis
terms.definition: The basis used to apply or evaluate a deductible.

terms.name: Deductible Amount
terms.definition: The monetary amount of a deductible.

terms.name: Deductible Percent
terms.definition: The percentage used to calculate a deductible.

terms.name: Minimum Deductible
terms.definition: The lowest deductible amount that can apply under the deductible terms.

terms.name: Maximum Deductible
terms.definition: The highest deductible amount that can apply under the deductible terms.

terms.name: Product Coverage
terms.definition: The many-to-many junction relating a marketed product to a reusable coverage definition. Carries product-coverage-specific defaults (selection, limits, deductibles), constraints (mandatory, minimum and maximum limits), and filing references.

terms.name: Default Selected Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator on a product-coverage record that the coverage is selected by default when the product is offered.

terms.name: Default Limit
terms.definition: The limit amount that applies by default when a product is sold under a particular product-coverage filing. Paired with a currency code.

terms.name: Default Deductible
terms.definition: The deductible amount that applies by default when a product is sold under a particular product-coverage filing. Paired with a currency code.

terms.name: Filing Reference
terms.definition: A form code, edition, or jurisdiction reference associated with a product-coverage offering when filings vary by jurisdiction or revision.

terms.name: Form Code
terms.definition: A filed form code associated with a product-coverage offering.

terms.name: Form Edition Code
terms.definition: A filed form edition or revision code associated with a product-coverage offering.

terms.name: Insurable Object
terms.definition: An object, property, vehicle, operation, interest, or location that may be insured.

terms.name: Insurable Object Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of insurable object represented.

terms.name: Insurable Object Classification
terms.definition: A durable classification used to organize insurable objects for underwriting, rating, reporting, or analytics.

terms.name: Classification Scheme
terms.definition: The business scheme or grouping from which an insurable object classification is drawn.

terms.name: Exposure
terms.definition: The measurable risk basis associated with a policy, coverage, claim, submission, underwriting, or analytical context.

terms.name: Exposure Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on an exposure record (`exposure_uid`). An immutable GUID used as the join key for every reference to the exposure.

terms.name: Exposure Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of risk basis represented.

terms.name: Exposure Basis
terms.definition: The basis used to measure exposure.

terms.name: Exposure Quantity
terms.definition: The measured amount of exposure.

terms.name: Exposure Unit
terms.definition: The unit of measure used for exposure quantity.

terms.name: Rating Territory
terms.definition: A geographic, regulatory, or business territory used in rating or risk evaluation.

terms.name: Geographic Location
terms.definition: A canonical location reference that can be associated with an exposure, insurable object, policy, claim, or other business context.

terms.name: Vehicle Exposure
terms.definition: Vehicle-specific exposure attributes linked to a canonical exposure.

terms.name: Vehicle Use
terms.definition: A classification of how a vehicle is used for insurance risk evaluation.

terms.name: Vehicle Class
terms.definition: A classification of a vehicle for underwriting, rating, reporting, or analytics.

terms.name: Garaging Location
terms.definition: The location where a vehicle is ordinarily kept or principally located.

terms.name: Radius
terms.definition: A classification or measure describing the operating radius for a vehicle exposure.

terms.name: Stated Value
terms.definition: The value stated for a vehicle or other insured item when used as an exposure or coverage basis.

terms.name: Property Exposure
terms.definition: Property-specific exposure attributes linked to a canonical exposure.

terms.name: Property Use
terms.definition: A classification of how property is used for insurance risk evaluation.

terms.name: Occupancy Type
terms.definition: A classification describing occupancy of a property.

terms.name: Construction Type
terms.definition: A classification describing the construction characteristics of a property.

terms.name: Protection Class
terms.definition: A classification used to represent fire protection, emergency response, or other protective context for a property exposure.

terms.name: Building Value
terms.definition: The monetary value associated with the building portion of a property exposure.

terms.name: Contents Value
terms.definition: The monetary value associated with contents for a property exposure.

terms.name: Workers Compensation Exposure
terms.definition: Workers compensation-specific exposure attributes linked to a canonical exposure.

terms.name: Governing Class
terms.definition: The classification treated as the primary workers compensation classification for a risk context.

terms.name: Job Duty Description
terms.definition: A business description of work duties associated with a workers compensation exposure.

terms.name: Payroll Amount
terms.definition: Payroll used as an exposure measure for workers compensation risk.

terms.name: Employee Count
terms.definition: The number of employees associated with a workers compensation exposure.

terms.name: Full Time Equivalent Count
terms.definition: The employee count normalized to a full-time equivalent basis.

terms.name: Payroll Period
terms.definition: The date range for payroll used in a workers compensation exposure.

terms.name: Financial Transaction
terms.definition: Monetary activity associated with policy, claim, coverage, party, exposure, accounting, or other Property and Casualty business context.

terms.name: Financial Transaction Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on a financial transaction record (`financial_transaction_uid`). An immutable GUID used as the join key for every reference to the transaction.

terms.name: Transaction Number
terms.definition: The business-friendly reference the source system or business operations assigns to a financial transaction. Distinct from the financial transaction identifier; not used as the primary key or relationship join key.

terms.name: Transaction Type
terms.definition: A classification of operational or financial activity.

terms.name: Transaction Classification
terms.definition: A more specific classification that supports analysis of monetary activity without creating a separate contract for every money subtype.

terms.name: Transaction Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a financial transaction.

terms.name: Transaction Effective Date
terms.definition: The date when the transaction takes business effect.

terms.name: Transaction Posted Date
terms.definition: The date when the transaction is posted to an accounting or reporting context.

terms.name: Accounting Period
terms.definition: The accounting or reporting period associated with a financial transaction.

terms.name: Transaction Amount
terms.definition: The monetary amount of a financial transaction.

terms.name: Transaction Currency
terms.definition: The currency in which the transaction amount is stated.

terms.name: Debit Credit Code
terms.definition: A classification that indicates whether a transaction is treated as a debit or credit in the relevant accounting context.

terms.name: Source Transaction Reference
terms.definition: A source-neutral reference that helps trace or reconcile a financial transaction without making the canonical contract source-specific.

terms.name: Premium
terms.definition: Money charged or recognized for insurance coverage.

terms.name: Fee
terms.definition: Money charged for a service, process, or policy-related item that is not the core premium.

terms.name: Tax
terms.definition: Money charged or collected for a tax obligation associated with insurance activity.

terms.name: Surcharge
terms.definition: An additional charge applied to insurance activity according to a business, regulatory, or product rule.

terms.name: Commission
terms.definition: Money associated with compensation for producer, broker, agency, or other distribution participation.

terms.name: Payment
terms.definition: Money transferred to satisfy premium, claim, fee, recovery, or other financial obligation.

terms.name: Reserve
terms.definition: Money estimated or held for expected claim responsibility.

terms.name: Deductible Recovery
terms.definition: Money recovered from an insured to satisfy a deductible obligation under a coverage.

terms.name: Reinsurance Recovery
terms.definition: Money recovered under a reinsurance arrangement in connection with a primary loss. The structural reinsurance contract family is deferred per `references/design-decisions/pc/risk-transfer-scope.md`; reinsurance-recovery activity that flows through carrier financial systems can be represented today as a financial-transaction classification.

terms.name: Loss Payment
terms.definition: A financial transaction that pays loss amounts under a claim, distinct from expense payments.

terms.name: Expense Payment
terms.definition: A financial transaction that pays expense amounts associated with claim handling, distinct from loss payments.

terms.name: Loss Reserve
terms.definition: Money estimated or held for expected loss responsibility on a claim.

terms.name: Expense Reserve
terms.definition: Money estimated or held for expected expense responsibility on a claim, distinct from loss reserves.

terms.name: Transaction Immutability
terms.definition: The convention that a financial transaction row is never updated in place. Corrections are emitted as new transaction rows with `correction_indicator` set to true and `corrects_*_uid` referencing the corrected row. See `cross-cutting.md` for the broader event-and-transaction convention.

terms.name: Policy
terms.definition: A durable insurance contract identity and current policy summary for Property and Casualty business.

terms.name: Policy Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on a policy record (`policy_uid`). An immutable GUID generated upstream and used as the join key for every reference to the policy.

terms.name: Policy Number
terms.definition: The business-friendly identifier the business or operations assigns to a policy. Distinct from the policy identifier; not used as the primary key or relationship join key.

terms.name: Policy Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a policy.

terms.name: Policy Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of policy represented.

terms.name: Line Of Business
terms.definition: A grouping of insurance business based on the risk or coverage domain, such as auto, property, liability, workers compensation, or another recognized P&C line.

terms.name: Product
terms.definition: An insurance offering or product context used to organize policies, coverages, jurisdictions, and line-of-business applicability.

terms.name: Issuing Jurisdiction
terms.definition: The jurisdiction whose rules, forms, or authority apply to issuance of a policy or product.

terms.name: Original Effective Date
terms.definition: The first date the policy became effective as a durable insurance contract.

terms.name: Issue Date
terms.definition: The date when the policy was issued.

terms.name: Current Policy Term
terms.definition: The policy term currently associated with the policy summary.

terms.name: Prior Policy
terms.definition: A previous policy related to the current policy, often through renewal, rewrite, replacement, or similar continuity.

terms.name: Policy Term
terms.definition: A bounded period of coverage or policy activity associated with a policy.

terms.name: Policy Party Role
terms.definition: The participation of a party in a policy context.

terms.name: Policy Term Number
terms.definition: A business-facing sequence or number that identifies a term for a policy.

terms.name: Term Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a policy term.

terms.name: Term Effective Date
terms.definition: The date when a policy term starts.

terms.name: Term Expiration Date
terms.definition: The date when a policy term ends.

terms.name: Cancellation Date
terms.definition: The date when a policy term or policy context is cancelled.

terms.name: Renewal
terms.definition: Continuation of policy coverage into a new policy term or related policy period.

terms.name: Annualized Premium
terms.definition: Premium expressed as an annual amount for comparison, reporting, or policy summary context.

terms.name: Premium Currency
terms.definition: The currency in which premium amounts are stated.

terms.name: Policy Lifecycle Event
terms.definition: A meaningful event that records progress or change in a policy lifecycle.

terms.name: Policy Transaction
terms.definition: Transaction-level policy activity with business meaning, such as endorsement, renewal, cancellation, reinstatement, audit, or another policy change process.

terms.name: Transaction Sequence Number
terms.definition: A sequence used to order policy transactions within a policy or term context.

terms.name: Transaction Processed Datetime
terms.definition: The date and time when a policy transaction was processed or recorded.

terms.name: Premium Change Amount
terms.definition: The monetary change in premium associated with a policy transaction.

terms.name: Requested By Party
terms.definition: The party that requested a policy transaction.

terms.name: Processed By Party
terms.definition: The party that processed or is accountable for a policy transaction.

terms.name: Policy Document
terms.definition: A document associated with a policy, policy term, or policy transaction.

terms.name: Bind
terms.definition: A business event or state in which coverage is committed before or as part of policy issuance.

terms.name: Policy Issue
terms.definition: A lifecycle event or activity that creates the issued policy record or makes the policy available as an issued contract.

terms.name: Endorsement
terms.definition: A policy change that modifies policy terms, coverages, parties, limits, deductibles, exposures, or related details after initial issue.

terms.name: Reinstatement
terms.definition: Restoration of policy effectiveness after cancellation, lapse, or another inactive state.

terms.name: Non-Renewal
terms.definition: A decision or event indicating that a policy will not continue into another term.

terms.name: Rewrite
terms.definition: A policy lifecycle activity that replaces or restates policy context through a new or related policy.

terms.name: Audit
terms.definition: A review activity that may adjust policy, exposure, premium, or related details after issue or during the policy lifecycle.

terms.name: Reference Data
terms.definition: Canonical coded or descriptive values used consistently across contracts. Includes both governed codeset contracts (where each row is a code value with a label, optional external-standard mapping, and SCD2 history) and entity-like reference contracts such as `GeographicLocation` and `LocationAddress`.

terms.name: Codeset Contract
terms.definition: A small, governed reference-data contract whose rows enumerate the allowed values for a `*_code` field. Every codeset has the same uniform shape: a system identity column, `code_value`, `code_label`, `code_description`, optional external standard mapping, and SCD2 system-time fields. See `cross-cutting.md` for the broader codeset strategy.

terms.name: External Standard
terms.definition: The external standards body or specification (such as ACORD, NAIC, ISO 4217, or ISO 3166-2) whose code is captured in the codeset's `external_standard_code` field.

terms.name: Reference Status
terms.definition: The lifecycle state of a reference data value.

terms.name: Active Status Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that a lifecycle status represents an active or in-force state.

terms.name: Terminal Status Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that a lifecycle status represents an ending state for the relevant lifecycle.

terms.name: Lifecycle Status
terms.definition: A reusable lifecycle state for a business subject such as submission, policy, term, coverage, claim, assessment, document, party, or transaction.

terms.name: Lifecycle Subject
terms.definition: The business subject to which a lifecycle status or lifecycle event type applies.

terms.name: Lifecycle Event Type
terms.definition: A reusable classification of a meaningful lifecycle event.

terms.name: Resulting Lifecycle Status
terms.definition: The lifecycle status that normally follows a lifecycle event type.

terms.name: Transaction Type Reference
terms.definition: Reference data that classifies operational or financial activity.

terms.name: Transaction Category
terms.definition: A broader grouping of transaction types.

terms.name: Financial Transaction Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that a transaction type is used for monetary activity.

terms.name: Lifecycle Event Indicator
terms.definition: An indicator that a transaction type is also used to describe or support lifecycle activity.

terms.name: Line Of Business Reference
terms.definition: Reference data that defines a recognized Property and Casualty line of business.

terms.name: Business Segment
terms.definition: A grouping used to organize lines of business for management, reporting, or product context.

terms.name: Parent Line Of Business
terms.definition: A higher-level line of business used to organize more specific lines.

terms.name: Geographic Location Reference
terms.definition: Reference data that identifies a place or geographic area used across insurance contexts.

terms.name: Location Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of location represented.

terms.name: Country Subdivision
terms.definition: A state, province, territory, or other subdivision within a country.

terms.name: Geocode Precision
terms.definition: A classification of how precise a latitude and longitude are for a location.

terms.name: Location Address
terms.definition: Address detail associated with a geographic location.

terms.name: Address Type
terms.definition: A classification of the business use or form of an address.

terms.name: Record Status Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates warehouse-level record states. Allowed values include `ACTIVE`, `SUPERSEDED`, `SOFT_DELETED`, `RESTATED`, and `MERGED`. Referenced from every entity contract's `record_status_code` field.

terms.name: Currency Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates currencies used in monetary fields across the contract set. Mapped to the ISO 4217 standard. Referenced from every `*_currency_code` field.

terms.name: Jurisdiction Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates jurisdictions in which insurance contracts are issued, governed, or regulated. Mapped to ISO 3166-2 where applicable.

terms.name: Policy Status Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates policy lifecycle status values such as quoted, bound, issued, in-force, cancelled, lapsed, expired, and reinstated.

terms.name: Policy Type Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates policy classification values such as new business, renewal, rewrite, and replacement.

terms.name: Term Status Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates policy term lifecycle status values such as pending, active, cancelled, expired, and replaced.

terms.name: Coverage Basis Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates coverage basis classifications used to apply a coverage within a policy context.

terms.name: Coverage Level Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates the level at which a coverage applies, such as policy, term, location, item, exposure, or coverage part.

terms.name: Coverage Status Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates the lifecycle status of a coverage within a policy context.

terms.name: Party Type Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates party classification values such as person, organization, household, and trust.

terms.name: Party Role Type Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates party role types used across submission, policy, claim, coverage, and insurable-object role contracts.

terms.name: Claim Status Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates claim lifecycle status values such as open, closed, reopened, denied, and withdrawn.

terms.name: Cause Of Loss Code
terms.definition: The codeset that enumerates causes of loss associated with a claim or claim feature.

terms.name: Submission
terms.definition: A pre-policy insurance request or application that is being evaluated for quote, bind, decline, withdrawal, or later policy issuance.

terms.name: Submission Identifier
terms.definition: The system identity column on a submission record (`submission_uid`). An immutable GUID used as the join key for every reference to the submission.

terms.name: Submission Number
terms.definition: The business-friendly identifier the business or operations assigns to a submission. Distinct from the submission identifier; not used as the primary key or relationship join key.

terms.name: Submission Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a submission.

terms.name: Submission Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of submission being evaluated.

terms.name: Received Date
terms.definition: The date when the submission was received for intake or evaluation.

terms.name: Requested Effective Date
terms.definition: The date when the requester wants coverage or policy activity to become effective.

terms.name: Quote Date
terms.definition: The date when a quote or price indication is provided for a submission.

terms.name: Bind Date
terms.definition: The date when coverage is bound or committed for a submission, subject to the applicable business process.

terms.name: Decline Date
terms.definition: The date when the submission is declined.

terms.name: Withdrawn Date
terms.definition: The date when the submission is withdrawn from consideration.

terms.name: Related Policy
terms.definition: A policy connected to a submission, usually after bind, issue, renewal, or another policy-forming activity.

terms.name: Submission Party Role
terms.definition: The participation of a party in a submission context.

terms.name: Submission Risk
terms.definition: Risk information presented or evaluated as part of a submission.

terms.name: Requested Coverage
terms.definition: Coverage requested or indicated for a submitted risk.

terms.name: Submission Assessment
terms.definition: An underwriting, triage, clearance, referral, or risk evaluation activity performed within a submission.

terms.name: Assessment Type
terms.definition: A classification of the kind of assessment performed on a submission or submitted risk.

terms.name: Assessment Status
terms.definition: The current lifecycle state of a submission assessment.

terms.name: Assessment Result
terms.definition: The outcome or conclusion of a submission assessment.

terms.name: Referral
terms.definition: An indication that a submission or submitted risk requires review by a person, team, or process beyond the initial handling path.

terms.name: Assessment Summary
terms.definition: A concise business summary of the assessment result or rationale.

terms.name: Submission Document
terms.definition: A document associated with a submission, such as supporting information, forms, correspondence, or issued material.

terms.name: Document Reference
terms.definition: A source-neutral pointer or reference to where a document can be found or retrieved.

terms.name: Required Document
terms.definition: A document expected or required for submission evaluation or completion.

terms.name: Submission Lifecycle Event
terms.definition: A meaningful event that changes or records progress in the submission lifecycle.

terms.name: Prior Status
terms.definition: The lifecycle status before a lifecycle event occurred.

terms.name: Resulting Status
terms.definition: The lifecycle status after a lifecycle event occurred.

terms.name: Initiating Party
terms.definition: The party that started, requested, or caused a lifecycle event.
